standard.title: Organise information and data
standard.description: locate, collect and organise information and data from primary and secondary sources in a range of formats
standard.prior_knowledge: From AC9HS5S02 (Organise primary and secondary sources): Students can locate, collect and organise information from primary and secondary sources using a range of graphic organisers, maps, timelines and graphs with appropriate conventions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate, collect and organise information and data from primary and secondary sources in a range of formats, using appropriate methods including digital tools, fieldwork, surveys and spatial technologies.

nodes.label: Selecting appropriate methods for collecting information
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can determine the most appropriate method for finding information for a specific inquiry purpose, selecting from personal observation, interviews, surveys, internet searches, census data, and primary and secondary sources.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the most appropriate method for finding information for one inquiry purpose and explain why it is the best choice.
nodes.typical_width: Determine appropriate information-collection methods for different inquiry purposes: personal observation, interviews, surveys, internet searches, census data, library catalogues, excursions and field trips — and explain why different methods are more appropriate for different types of questions.
wider: Compare the information yielded by two different collection methods for the same inquiry question (e.g. survey vs interview) and evaluate what each reveals and omits
Plan and conduct a field trip or excursion (virtual or actual) to collect primary data for a HASS inquiry, applying appropriate observation and recording strategies
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who always default to internet search as their collection method will miss the richer data that surveys, interviews, fieldwork and census data provide. Method selection is the first decision that shapes what evidence is available for analysis.

response_modes.reason: Use a method-selection decision framework: What kind of question is this? What kind of data would answer it? Which collection method produces that data? Apply to multiple inquiry examples before students make independent choices.

success_criteria: Students identify an appropriate collection method for at least two different inquiry purposes.
Students explain why each method is the best choice for the inquiry type.

nodes.label: Evaluating sources and identifying key words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use key words to search for relevant information and evaluate sources, recognising that domain names (com, edu, gov) indicate source provenance.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify appropriate search keywords for an inquiry and explain what domain names (com, edu, gov) indicate about source provenance.
nodes.typical_width: Identify key words for effective information searches using search engines and library catalogues; evaluate sources using domain names as provenance indicators (com = commercial, edu = educational, gov = government); assess source relevance and reliability.
wider: Develop and apply an advanced search strategy (including Boolean operators and domain filtering) to find high-quality sources for a specific HASS inquiry
Evaluate the difference between search results from edu/gov sources versus com sources on the same topic — and assess what each reveals about perspective and reliability

response_modes.reason: Digital search skills degrade without consistent practice — key word selection and domain-based provenance evaluation need to be applied regularly across inquiry tasks, not just taught once.

success_criteria: Students identify appropriate keywords for at least one HASS inquiry search.
Students correctly explain what edu, gov and com domain names indicate about a source.

nodes.label: Creating maps and spatial representations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create maps using spatial technologies and cartographic conventions appropriate to the inquiry purpose, including flow maps and large-scale location maps.
nodes.minimum_width: Create one map using appropriate cartographic conventions (border, source, scale, legend, title, north point) relevant to a HASS inquiry.
nodes.typical_width: Create maps using spatial technologies and cartographic conventions — including large-scale location maps (places and features in Australia and Asia) and flow maps (showing connections such as shipping routes or migration flows) — applying all required conventions correctly.
wider: Create a digital map using spatial technologies to display Year 6 inquiry data (e.g. Australia's connections with Asia, migration patterns, three levels of government jurisdictions) and explain the design choices made
Compare a hand-drawn map with a digital map of the same information and evaluate the advantages of each medium for communication

response_modes.reason: Cartographic conventions require precision and consistent practice — particularly flow maps, which are a new format at Year 6. Errors in conventions undermine geographic communication.

success_criteria: Students create at least one map with all required cartographic conventions applied correctly.
The map communicates HASS data relevant to the inquiry purpose.

nodes.label: Organising multi-source information for a Year 6 inquiry
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can locate, collect and organise information and data from multiple primary and secondary sources in a range of formats, selecting appropriate tools and applying relevant conventions.
nodes.minimum_width: Collect information from at least two different source types and organise it using at least two appropriate organisational tools.
nodes.typical_width: Locate, collect and organise information from a range of sources (internet, primary sources, surveys, census data, field work, visual materials) for a Year 6 HASS inquiry; select appropriate organisational tools (maps, timelines, flow charts, tables, bibliography templates); apply relevant conventions throughout.
wider: Design a complete information organisation system for a complex Year 6 inquiry — specifying which tools will be used for which information and why
Evaluate the organisation of a completed inquiry — assess whether the tools chosen made the information accessible and useful, and identify improvements

response_modes.reason: Organising multi-source information at Year 6 requires deliberate planning — students need to make conscious decisions about tools, formats and conventions before collecting, not after. Scaffold the planning phase.

success_criteria: Students collect information from at least two source types for a HASS inquiry.
Students organise information using at least two appropriate tools with relevant conventions applied.
Students explain why they selected the tools they used.
